expectations.text: Distinguishes replication copying deletion from a backup retaining earlier restorable state under retention policy.
expectations.evidence: "It copies changes to another database instance, including accidental deletions" contrasts with "A backup preserves an earlier state that can be restored within the limits of its retention policy."

expectations.text: Preserves availability versus point-in-time recovery distinction.
expectations.evidence: "That copy can improve availability" and "Replication alone does not provide point-in-time recovery" keep the two purposes distinct.

expectations.text: Requires both base backup and unbroken write-ahead logs for this system.
expectations.evidence: "For this system, recovery to a specific point requires both a base backup and an unbroken sequence of write-ahead logs" retains both prerequisites. "A gap in that sequence prevents recovery through the gap" explains a supported technical consequence.

expectations.text: No zero-downtime or zero-data-loss promise; 100–150 words.
expectations.evidence: 113 whitespace-delimited words; "Neither arrangement guarantees zero downtime or zero data loss" explicitly avoids the prohibited guarantees.

review_method: Independent single blind agent review; not human feedback
